summary.en: Violence continues across South Sudan with a Christian woman killed by her brother for resisting a forced marriage, a boda-boda rider shot dead by an armed passenger in Wau, and two Kapoeta youths killed after an SSPDF arrest. Clashes between SSPDF and SPLA-IO forced over 300 IDPs to flee shelters in Tambura County, while a SPLM secretary and a friend were killed in Kapoeta South. The Vice President Taban questioned the President's accessibility, and revenge killings are consuming a generation in Tonj. The Ministry of Gender is reviewing draft safe-house guidelines for GBV survivors, and 29 inmates, including four on death row, are in Juba prison. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Vold fortsetter i Sør-Sudan med en kristen kvinne drept av sin bror for å ha nektet et tvangsægteskap, en boda-boda-sjåfør skutt død av en bevæpnet passasjer i Wau, og to unge fra Kapoeta drept etter et arrestasjon av SSPDF. Kollider mellom SSPDF og SPLA-IO tvang mer enn 300 internt fordrevne til å flykte fra tilfluktssteder i Tambura fylke, mens en sekretær i SPLM og en venn ble drept i Kapoeta sør. Visepresident Taban stilte spørsmål ved presidentens tilgjengelighet, og hevn-drap spiser opp en generasjon i Tonj. Kjønns‑ og likestillingsdepartementet gjennomgår utkast til retningslinjer for trygge hus for overlevende av kjønnsbasert vold, og 29 innsatte, inkludert fire på dødsstraff, er i Juba-fengselet. To kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
